rating.verdict: Solid midrange with plenty of removal and a real sideboard. Good enough for FNM, but slower and less tuned than the top Standard decks.
strengths: Deep removal suite answers most threats
Picard, Officer tokens and ships win the long game
Sideboard covers aggro, control and artifacts
weaknesses: Can fall behind against fast, wide aggro
Few ways to close a game quickly

wins: Midrange: trade your removal for their best threats, then win the long game with Captain Picard, his Officer tokens and your ships.
plan: Develop Vexing Drone, Picard (Leading by Example) or Troi. Zero, Incorporeal Sensate looks at their hand and exiles their best card.
Answer whatever matters with the right tool (see key cards). Land Captain Picard when the board is safe.
U.S.S. Excelsior kills a tapped creature on arrival, Enterprise-A adds three Officers, Constable Odo stuns their best attacker. Big creatures can instead cycle for a land early.
keys: Answers hexproof and ward (edict) or swarms of tokens (-1/-1 to all others). Pick the mode the board needs.
Exiles any creature or Spacecraft, including artifact creatures that Resistance Is Futile can’t hit.
A three-chapter edict, card and token engine. Great against a single big threat.
Exiles any nonland permanent: enchantments, ships, planeswalkers.
tips: Don’t spend removal on every 1/1. Save it for creatures that actually threaten you.
Impossible Choice gives the opponent two 1/1 Officers when it destroys. Use it on something big, or take the draw-two mode.
Resistance Is Futile can’t target artifact creatures.
Set Phasers’ 3-damage mode only hits attackers; the stun mode hits anything.
Free Borg Revolutionaries and Rogue Artificial Intelligence cycle for 2 to find a basic land when you’re short.
mulligan: Keep 3–4 lands with a mix of creatures and removal. Two-landers need cheap plays.
sideboard: Command Decision, Eject the Warp Core
